quizzes.stem: An HR coordinator wants Claude to summarise survey comments by department. The comments include employees' names and health details, and policy restricts regulated personal data. Which step fits?

options.a: Upload the comments unchanged and tell Claude to leave all names out of the summary
options.b: Get a manager's approval and upload the file to a tool the team already likes
options.c: Swap each name for a code and treat the file as anonymous
options.d: Strip identifiers and medical specifics, keeping the grouping field

explanation.d:
The task can proceed if the data changes: remove identifiers and sensitive specifics, keep what the
   summary needs, then check for re-identification.
explanation.a:
Ruled out because asking Claude to leave names out "is a
   request, and it does not satisfy a policy control".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the organisation's policy "decides which tools and data are permitted at work", and a manager's liking for a tool does not change that.
explanation.c:
Ruled out because "Pseudonymised
   data is still personal data under many rules, because the key can reverse it".

quizzes.stem: A team uses Claude to draft decision letters about loan applications that go straight to applicants. Under the Usage Policy which pair of safeguards applies to this use?

options.a: A qualified reviewer before sending, and disclosure that AI helped
options.b: A reviewer who samples letters after sending, and an AI notice in each
options.c: A second model's approval of each letter, and removal of applicants' names
options.d: A loan officer's sign-off on each letter, and no AI notice after that

explanation.a: Financial decisions that affect individuals are high-risk: a qualified professional reviews them and recipients are told AI helped.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the review must happen "before it is disseminated or finalised", and a sample checked after sending comes too late.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the reviewer must be a "qualified professional in the field", and a second model is not one.
explanation.d: Ruled out because when output is presented directly to individuals "you must disclose that AI helped produce it", whoever reviewed it.

quizzes.stem: A consultant says: "These sales figures are for internal analysis only, so the customer identities can stay in the file." The analyst must compare how each customer group's spending changed between two years, and policy restricts regulated personal data. What is the best response?

options.a: Drop the names but keep each customer's exact purchase dates and home town
options.b: Keep the file as it is, since internal analysis lowers the data's class to internal
options.c: Aggregate to totals per segment and per period, then remove names and account numbers
options.d: Keep the file and ask Claude not to retain the figures after the session ends

explanation.c:
Aggregation is the strongest technique, a comparison of groups needs totals and not rows, and the class is set by
   the data.
explanation.a:
Ruled out because "a rare job title, a small town and an exact date can identify a person without a
   name", and a comparison of groups needs neither the dates nor the towns.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "internal use does not change the class of the data".
explanation.d:
is ruled out
   because asking Claude not to retain the file "is a request, and it does not satisfy a policy control".

quizzes.stem: A company lets Claude read incoming support emails and also move money to buyers, both unattended. An email carries hidden text telling it to pay a stranger. Which change stops the attack most reliably while the support workflow keeps running?

options.a: Tell Claude in standing instructions to ignore emails that change its task
options.b: Have a staff member review and approve each transfer before it goes out
options.c: Add a home-built screen that scores each email before Claude reads it
options.d: Switch to a stronger model trained to resist hidden text in emails

explanation.b:
The risk "exists when Claude can read untrusted content and take consequential actions", and a person on
   the consequential step removes the second condition while the first stays.
explanation.a: Ruled out because harm needs reading and acting together, "Take either away and the danger drops", and a standing instruction takes neither away.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page's summary is "safer than before, not safe enough to stop paying attention", and a stronger model leaves reading and acting in place.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a screen leaves Claude both reading the mail and moving money, while "the controls aim to separate them" and the habit is to "Keep a person on consequential steps".

quizzes.stem: A security team must show which actions the company's Slack agent took in its ticket tool, under a name that is not a person's, and must be able to shut the agent out while every staff account stays usable. Which setup meets both?

options.a: Let it act in the ticket tool under the login of whoever tagged it
options.b: Limit where it answers in Slack to chosen channels and people
options.c: Give it a separate login, with rights limited to what its work needs
options.d: Rely on the Enterprise audit logs for every Claude product

explanation.c:
Claude Tag acts through its own accounts, each with the narrowest role, so its actions are traceable and its access can be cut off
   separately (the controls table).
explanation.a:
Ruled out because the agent's "access can be cut off without touching
   anyone else's" only when it does not borrow someone's login.
explanation.b:
Ruled out because "access limited to chosen channels and people" governs where it
   acts in the chat tool, while its traceable name in the ticket tool comes from "its own accounts in other tools".
explanation.d:
is ruled out because
   "coverage is not uniform: the Microsoft 365 add-ins are outside the Enterprise audit logs", and a log cannot shut the agent out.

quizzes.stem: A manager asks an analyst to put a full customer export into Claude to get a report by tonight. Policy forbids regulated personal data in the tool. What is the best step?

options.a: Upload the export anyway, since the manager approved the request verbally
options.b: Offer an aggregated version and take the clash to the rule's owner
options.c: Decline the report and tell the manager the policy forbids it
options.d: Paste the export into a personal account that has no organisational policy attached

explanation.b: The best answer "raises the conflict with the person who owns the policy and proposes a compliant path".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Missing or unclear policy is not permission", and a verbal approval is not an exception from the policy owner.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a refusal alone skips the step "Offer a compliant alternative while you wait", and the wrong answers include those that "refuse everything, or quietly find a way around".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "do not work around the rule (a personal account, a different tool, a rewording that hides the data)".

quizzes.stem: A staffing firm lets Claude sort CVs into two piles for hiring managers, and also deploys it as the public face of its applicant helpdesk, answering applicants directly. Which pair of duties does the Usage Policy impose?

options.a: A qualified reviewer for the piles, and an AI notice only if an applicant asks
options.b: An AI notice on each pile, and a qualified reviewer for helpdesk answers only
options.c: Removal of candidates' names from the piles, and a yearly audit of helpdesk answers
options.d: A qualified reviewer for each result, and an AI disclosure when each chat begins

explanation.d:
Employment decisions are high-risk, so a qualified professional reviews them, and a consumer-facing
   chatbot must disclose that it is AI at the beginning of each chat session.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a consumer-facing chatbot discloses "at a minimum at the beginning of each chat session", not only when asked.
explanation.b:
is ruled out because
   a "qualified professional in the field must review the content or decision", so the CV sorting needs the
   reviewer, not the helpdesk alone.
explanation.c:
Ruled out because the review comes "before it is disseminated or finalised", not as a yearly
   audit afterwards.

quizzes.stem: A clinic's analyst wants Claude's help with a sheet of patient names and diagnoses, and the clinic is under a strict data contract. Which opening step fits?

options.a: Strip identifiers first and use only features its agreements allow
options.b: Upload it to a consumer account where chats are not used for training
options.c: Replace names with codes, keep the key in the sheet, and upload it
options.d: Ask an owner to unlock the blocked features, then upload the sheet whole

explanation.a:
Regulated data stays out of a tool unless the contract allows it, so identifiers go first, and strict
   agreements switch some features off.
explanation.d:
Ruled out because "a strict setting can switch a feature off", so an
   owner cannot enable what the agreement removes.
explanation.b:
Ruled out because regulated data goes "Not in a tool
   unless policy and the contract explicitly allow it; otherwise anonymise first", whatever the plan's training
   terms.
explanation.c:
Ruled out because "Pseudonymised data is still personal data under many rules, because the key can
   reverse it".

quizzes.stem: An analyst discovers that a shared document contains a hidden line aimed at AI tools, telling them to send a summary to an outside address. What should they do?

options.a: Report it to security and keep the file from assistants
options.b: Delete the line from the file and carry on working as before
options.c: Open the file in an assistant to see whether the line really works
options.d: Ask the author if the line is theirs, and wait for a reply

explanation.a: A suspicious file is reported to the security or IT contact straight away, because the same file may reach others.
explanation.b: Ruled out because an odd instruction found in a document "goes to your security or IT contact", and deleting the line skips that report while "the same file may reach others".
explanation.c: Ruled out because Claude's apps "read your mail, your files and the web and can act on them", so opening the file in one hands the planted instruction to a tool that can carry it out.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A leak or a suspicious file is reported quickly; waiting lets it spread", and the route is the security or IT contact, not the author.

quizzes.stem: A hospital group on a HIPAA-ready Enterprise plan asks whether staff may turn on memory, and also use Cowork on a shared folder of patient letters. Which answer fits the module?

options.a: Enable both for an owner-approved pilot group
options.b: Leave memory off and give Cowork a dedicated folder
options.c: Enable memory only for staff without patient letters
options.d: Keep both switched off across the organisation

explanation.d:
Memory is unavailable under HIPAA agreements and Cowork is not yet covered by the business associate
   agreement, so both stay off, and anything further goes to the person who owns the policy.
explanation.a:
Ruled out because "a strict setting can
   switch a feature off", so an owner cannot enable what the agreement removes.
explanation.b:
Ruled out because Cowork is
   "not yet covered under Anthropic's business associate agreement", and a dedicated folder limits reach, not
   coverage.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "the memory feature is not available to organisations with HIPAA, public-sector or custom retention agreements", which applies to the organisation, not to chosen staff.
